- **Branch**: `fix/1079-sdk-host-slice3` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +713
- **Deletions**: -252
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T09:54:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T09:54:56Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079

## Delivered (slice 3 — builder-owned jobs)

**The task/subagent/fabric complex moves into the capability-gated assembled set (PR #1230's first "Remaining" item); the CLI no longer passes `task`/monitoring as post-plan host tools nor hand-assembles the manager.**

- **`SubagentServices`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart`, new) — the typed bundle of genuinely shell-side glue: wake launcher, registry sink/source, heartbeat delivery + live thresholds, roles resolver, children's compaction choice, misuse-breaker switch, child-session factory, session-IO retry. Absent bundle = the capability run-narrows `off(reason: … subagentServices …)` like any missing platform service — the complex never half-wires.
- **`_wireFabric` / `_wireTaskSurface`** — the builder assembles the messaging fabric (file layer over `sessionRoot`; hub primary only when the hub transport survived run-narrowing; E1-loud when the hub wires without a `mainMailbox` resolver), then the `SubagentManager` → A2A gateway (a2a transport) → heartbeat (started, kill-switch aware) → `TaskToolConfig` (children draw the child-safe core list; live stream/model accessors) → monitoring tools → `task`, gated by `HostCapability.messagingFabric`/`HostCapability.subagents`.
- **Registry order preserved byte-identically**: `buildAgentStack` now emits core tools → gated task surface (monitoring, then `task` LAST) → residual `additionalTools` — exactly the pre-conversion registration order. The gated surface stays OUT of `WiredAgentCore.tools` (children must never draw it; the executor strips only `task` itself).
- **Catalog corrections** — `subagents` now requires `{sessionRoot, subagentServices}`; `messagingFabric`'s file transport declares `sessionRoot` per-transport (a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer).
- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). Net: the shell lost ~140 lines of hand-rolled assembly.
- **AGENTS.md** — the host-shell wiring rule now names the builder-owned task complex (conventions invariant).

## Remaining (later slices, per the issue)

- Checkpoint/roles/queue/approval/redaction post-construction attachments into the builder (slice 4).
- Model-facing emission through the plan (prompt sections/help driven by `surfacedTokens`).
- Remaining host shells (macOS/iOS/Android/web/extension/Outlook) consume `wireAgentCore`; config-section parity (#1078) generalizes onto the builder per OQ1.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The main checkout's system dart is unusable here (flutter shim dies on seatbelt-blocked engine-stamp writes; the bare VM is SIGKILLed with exit 137 by the machine guard — the known lane pitfall). Gates ran in the worktree via a sibling lane's temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + the fleet `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`:

- `dart test test/hosts/ test/parity/` — **80/80 green** (matrix completeness, E1/E2, AC7 hiding, parity guards).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` — **87/87 green** (the CLI constructor end-to-end over the moved wiring).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_agents_panel_test.dart test/task/subagent_lifecycle_test.dart` — **36/36 green** (registry persistence/rehydration through the builder-assembled manager; child resume/wake).
- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart test/hosts` — clean. `dart format` applied (3.13.4; it reflowed two pre-existing spots in the hosts test/catalog that the previous slice's formatter version had left non-canonical).

New tests fail-first: the slice-3 group was written before the implementation (absent-bundle narrowing, child-safety of the core list, canonical order, fabric composition, handle exposure, off-profile hiding) and went green with the builder changes.

- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). ## PR Description

Part of #1079

## Delivered (slice 3 — builder-owned jobs)

**The task/subagent/fabric complex moves into the capability-gated assembled set (PR #1230's first "Remaining" item); the CLI no longer passes `task`/monitoring as post-plan host tools nor hand-assembles the manager.**

- **`SubagentServices`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart`, new) — the typed bundle of genuinely shell-side glue: wake launcher, registry sink/source, heartbeat delivery + live thresholds, roles resolver, children's compaction choice, misuse-breaker switch, child-session factory, session-IO retry. Absent bundle = the capability run-narrows `off(reason: … subagentServices …)` like any missing platform service — the complex never half-wires.
- **`_wireFabric` / `_wireTaskSurface`** — the builder assembles the messaging fabric (file layer over `sessionRoot`; hub primary only when the hub transport survived run-narrowing; E1-loud when the hub wires without a `mainMailbox` resolver), then the `SubagentManager` → A2A gateway (a2a transport) → heartbeat (started, kill-switch aware) → `TaskToolConfig` (children draw the child-safe core list; live stream/model accessors) → monitoring tools → `task`, gated by `HostCapability.messagingFabric`/`HostCapability.subagents`.
- **Registry order preserved byte-identically**: `buildAgentStack` now emits core tools → gated task surface (monitoring, then `task` LAST) → residual `additionalTools` — exactly the pre-conversion registration order. The gated surface stays OUT of `WiredAgentCore.tools` (children must never draw it; the executor strips only `task` itself).
- **Catalog corrections** — `subagents` now requires `{sessionRoot, subagentServices}`; `messagingFabric`'s file transport declares `sessionRoot` per-transport (a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer).
- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). Net: the shell lost ~140 lines of hand-rolled assembly.
- **AGENTS.md** — the host-shell wiring rule now names the builder-owned task complex (conventions invariant).

## Remaining (later slices, per the issue)

- Checkpoint/roles/queue/approval/redaction post-construction attachments into the builder (slice 4).
- Model-facing emission through the plan (prompt sections/help driven by `surfacedTokens`).
- Remaining host shells (macOS/iOS/Android/web/extension/Outlook) consume `wireAgentCore`; config-section parity (#1078) generalizes onto the builder per OQ1.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The main checkout's system dart is unusable here (flutter shim dies on seatbelt-blocked engine-stamp writes; the bare VM is SIGKILLed with exit 137 by the machine guard — the known lane pitfall). Gates ran in the worktree via a sibling lane's temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + the fleet `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`:

- `dart test test/hosts/ test/parity/` — **80/80 green** (matrix completeness, E1/E2, AC7 hiding, parity guards).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` — **87/87 green** (the CLI constructor end-to-end over the moved wiring).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_agents_panel_test.dart test/task/subagent_lifecycle_test.dart` — **36/36 green** (registry persistence/rehydration through the builder-assembled manager; child resume/wake).
- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart test/hosts` — clean. `dart format` applied (3.13.4; it reflowed two pre-existing spots in the hosts test/catalog that the previous slice's formatter version had left non-canonical).

New tests fail-first: the slice-3 group was written before the implementation (absent-bundle narrowing, child-safety of the core list, canonical order, fabric composition, handle exposure, off-profile hiding) and went green with the builder changes.

## PR Description

Part of #1079

## Delivered (slice 3 — builder-owned jobs)

**The task/subagent/fabric complex moves into the capability-gated assembled set (PR #1230's first "Remaining" item); the CLI no longer passes `task`/monitoring as post-plan host tools nor hand-assembles the manager.**

- **`SubagentServices`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart`, new) — the typed bundle of genuinely shell-side glue: wake launcher, registry sink/source, heartbeat delivery + live thresholds, roles resolver, children's compaction choice, misuse-breaker switch, child-session factory, session-IO retry. Absent bundle = the capability run-narrows `off(reason: … subagentServices …)` like any missing platform service — the complex never half-wires.
- **`_wireFabric` / `_wireTaskSurface`** — the builder assembles the messaging fabric (file layer over `sessionRoot`; hub primary only when the hub transport survived run-narrowing; E1-loud when the hub wires without a `mainMailbox` resolver), then the `SubagentManager` → A2A gateway (a2a transport) → heartbeat (started, kill-switch aware) → `TaskToolConfig` (children draw the child-safe core list; live stream/model accessors) → monitoring tools → `task`, gated by `HostCapability.messagingFabric`/`HostCapability.subagents`.
- **Registry order preserved byte-identically**: `buildAgentStack` now emits core tools → gated task surface (monitoring, then `task` LAST) → residual `additionalTools` — exactly the pre-conversion registration order. The gated surface stays OUT of `WiredAgentCore.tools` (children must never draw it; the executor strips only `task` itself).
- **Catalog corrections** — `subagents` now requires `{sessionRoot, subagentServices}`; `messagingFabric`'s file transport declares `sessionRoot` per-transport (a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer).
- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). Net: the shell lost ~140 lines of hand-rolled assembly.
- **AGENTS.md** — the host-shell wiring rule now names the builder-owned task complex (conventions invariant).

## Remaining (later slices, per the issue)

- Checkpoint/roles/queue/approval/redaction post-construction attachments into the builder (slice 4).
- Model-facing emission through the plan (prompt sections/help driven by `surfacedTokens`).
- Remaining host shells (macOS/iOS/Android/web/extension/Outlook) consume `wireAgentCore`; config-section parity (#1078) generalizes onto the builder per OQ1.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The main checkout's system dart is unusable here (flutter shim dies on seatbelt-blocked engine-stamp writes; the bare VM is SIGKILLed with exit 137 by the machine guard — the known lane pitfall). Gates ran in the worktree via a sibling lane's temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + the fleet `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`:

- `dart test test/hosts/ test/parity/` — **80/80 green** (matrix completeness, E1/E2, AC7 hiding, parity guards).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` — **87/87 green** (the CLI constructor end-to-end over the moved wiring).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_agents_panel_test.dart test/task/subagent_lifecycle_test.dart` — **36/36 green** (registry persistence/rehydration through the builder-assembled manager; child resume/wake).
- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart test/hosts` — clean. `dart format` applied (3.13.4; it reflowed two pre-existing spots in the hosts test/catalog that the previous slice's formatter version had left non-canonical).

New tests fail-first: the slice-3 group was written before the implementation (absent-bundle narrowing, child-safety of the core list, canonical order, fabric composition, handle exposure, off-profile hiding) and went green with the builder changes.

The question is: is there a path where the hub primary calls `mainMailbox` BEFORE `_subagentManager` is assigned? Since `_subagentManager = wired.subagentManager!` is assigned right after `wireAgentCore` returns, and the closure is only invoked at mail time, it should be fine. But what if the CLI profile has `subagents` off (e.g. a config where subagents capability is off) while hubFabric is provided? Then `_wireFabric` wires the hub transport (messagingFabric wired) and `_subagentManager` stays null. Then when hub mail arrives, `() => _subagentManager.mailboxOf('main')` would throw a late-initialization error (or null check error) inside the hub primary's mail merge.   sessionRoot: config.sessionRoot,

content.text:
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface.

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release commits from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 ruleset-
  bypass App pushes the bump straight to protected main, so the App identity
  is what auditability hangs on.
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1313
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1313
- **Title**: feat(1079): SDK slice 3 — builder-owned task/subagent/fabric complex
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1079-sdk-host-slice3` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +713
- **Deletions**: -252
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T09:54:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T09:54:56Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079

## Delivered (slice 3 — builder-owned jobs)

**The task/subagent/fabric complex moves into the capability-gated assembled set (PR #1230's first "Remaining" item); the CLI no longer passes `task`/monitoring as post-plan host tools nor hand-assembles the manager.**

- **`SubagentServices`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart`, new) — the typed bundle of genuinely shell-side glue: wake launcher, registry sink/source, heartbeat delivery + live thresholds, roles resolver, children's compaction choice, misuse-breaker switch, child-session factory, session-IO retry. Absent bundle = the capability run-narrows `off(reason: … subagentServices …)` like any missing platform service — the complex never half-wires.
- **`_wireFabric` / `_wireTaskSurface`** — the builder assembles the messaging fabric (file layer over `sessionRoot`; hub primary only when the hub transport survived run-narrowing; E1-loud when the hub wires without a `mainMailbox` resolver), then the `SubagentManager` → A2A gateway (a2a transport) → heartbeat (started, kill-switch aware) → `TaskToolConfig` (children draw the child-safe core list; live stream/model accessors) → monitoring tools → `task`, gated by `HostCapability.messagingFabric`/`HostCapability.subagents`.
- **Registry order preserved byte-identically**: `buildAgentStack` now emits core tools → gated task surface (monitoring, then `task` LAST) → residual `additionalTools` — exactly the pre-conversion registration order. The gated surface stays OUT of `WiredAgentCore.tools` (children must never draw it; the executor strips only `task` itself).
- **Catalog corrections** — `subagents` now requires `{sessionRoot, subagentServices}`; `messagingFabric`'s file transport declares `sessionRoot` per-transport (a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer).
- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). Net: the shell lost ~140 lines of hand-rolled assembly.
- **AGENTS.md** — the host-shell wiring rule now names the builder-owned task complex (conventions invariant).

## Remaining (later slices, per the issue)

- Checkpoint/roles/queue/approval/redaction post-construction attachments into the builder (slice 4).
- Model-facing emission through the plan (prompt sections/help driven by `surfacedTokens`).
- Remaining host shells (macOS/iOS/Android/web/extension/Outlook) consume `wireAgentCore`; config-section parity (#1078) generalizes onto the builder per OQ1.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The main checkout's system dart is unusable here (flutter shim dies on seatbelt-blocked engine-stamp writes; the bare VM is SIGKILLed with exit 137 by the machine guard — the known lane pitfall). Gates ran in the worktree via a sibling lane's temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + the fleet `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`:

- `dart test test/hosts/ test/parity/` — **80/80 green** (matrix completeness, E1/E2, AC7 hiding, parity guards).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` — **87/87 green** (the CLI constructor end-to-end over the moved wiring).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_agents_panel_test.dart test/task/subagent_lifecycle_test.dart` — **36/36 green** (registry persistence/rehydration through the builder-assembled manager; child resume/wake).
- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart test/hosts` — clean. `dart format` applied (3.13.4; it reflowed two pre-existing spots in the hosts test/catalog that the previous slice's formatter version had left non-canonical).

New tests fail-first: the slice-3 group was written before the implementation (absent-bundle narrowing, child-safety of the core list, canonical order, fabric composition, handle exposure, off-profile hiding) and went green with the builder changes.

`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface.

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release commits from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 ruleset-
  bypass App pushes the bump straight to protected main, so the App identity
  is what auditability hangs on.
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +713
- **Deletions**: -252
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T09:54:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T09:54:56Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079

## Delivered (slice 3 — builder-owned jobs)

**The task/subagent/fabric complex moves into the capability-gated assembled set (PR #1230's first "Remaining" item); the CLI no longer passes `task`/monitoring as post-plan host tools nor hand-assembles the manager.**

- **`SubagentServices`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart`, new) — the typed bundle of genuinely shell-side glue: wake launcher, registry sink/source, heartbeat delivery + live thresholds, roles resolver, children's compaction choice, misuse-breaker switch, child-session factory, session-IO retry. Absent bundle = the capability run-narrows `off(reason: … subagentServices …)` like any missing platform service — the complex never half-wires.
- **`_wireFabric` / `_wireTaskSurface`** — the builder assembles the messaging fabric (file layer over `sessionRoot`; hub primary only when the hub transport survived run-narrowing; E1-loud when the hub wires without a `mainMailbox` resolver), then the `SubagentManager` → A2A gateway (a2a transport) → heartbeat (started, kill-switch aware) → `TaskToolConfig` (children draw the child-safe core list; live stream/model accessors) → monitoring tools → `task`, gated by `HostCapability.messagingFabric`/`HostCapability.subagents`.
- **Registry order preserved byte-identically**: `buildAgentStack` now emits core tools → gated task surface (monitoring, then `task` LAST) → residual `additionalTools` — exactly the pre-conversion registration order. The gated surface stays OUT of `WiredAgentCore.tools` (children must never draw it; the executor strips only `task` itself).
- **Catalog corrections** — `subagents` now requires `{sessionRoot, subagentServices}`; `messagingFabric`'s file transport declares `sessionRoot` per-transport (a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer).
- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). Net: the shell lost ~140 lines of hand-rolled assembly.
- **AGENTS.md** — the host-shell wiring rule now names the builder-owned task complex (conventions invariant).

## Remaining (later slices, per the issue)

- Checkpoint/roles/queue/approval/redaction post-construction attachments into the builder (slice 4).
- Model-facing emission through the plan (prompt sections/help driven by `surfacedTokens`).
- Remaining host shells (macOS/iOS/Android/web/extension/Outlook) consume `wireAgentCore`; config-section parity (#1078) generalizes onto the builder per OQ1.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The main checkout's system dart is unusable here (flutter shim dies on seatbelt-blocked engine-stamp writes; the bare VM is SIGKILLed with exit 137 by the machine guard — the known lane pitfall). Gates ran in the worktree via a sibling lane's temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + the fleet `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`:

- `dart test test/hosts/ test/parity/` — **80/80 green** (matrix completeness, E1/E2, AC7 hiding, parity guards).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` — **87/87 green** (the CLI constructor end-to-end over the moved wiring).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_agents_panel_test.dart test/task/subagent_lifecycle_test.dart` — **36/36 green** (registry persistence/rehydration through the builder-assembled manager; child resume/wake).
- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart test/hosts` — clean. `dart format` applied (3.13.4; it reflowed two pre-existing spots in the hosts test/catalog that the previous slice's formatter version had left non-canonical).

New tests fail-first: the slice-3 group was written before the implementation (absent-bundle narrowing, child-safety of the core list, canonical order, fabric composition, handle exposure, off-profile hiding) and went green with the builder changes.

`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface.

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate

  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 ruleset-
  bypass App pushes the bump straight to protected main, so the App identity

- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev

## PR Description

Part of #1079

## Delivered (slice 3 — builder-owned jobs)

**The task/subagent/fabric complex moves into the capability-gated assembled set (PR #1230's first "Remaining" item); the CLI no longer passes `task`/monitoring as post-plan host tools nor hand-assembles the manager.**

- **`SubagentServices`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart`, new) — the typed bundle of genuinely shell-side glue: wake launcher, registry sink/source, heartbeat delivery + live thresholds, roles resolver, children's compaction choice, misuse-breaker switch, child-session factory, session-IO retry. Absent bundle = the capability run-narrows `off(reason: … subagentServices …)` like any missing platform service — the complex never half-wires.
- **`_wireFabric` / `_wireTaskSurface`** — the builder assembles the messaging fabric (file layer over `sessionRoot`; hub primary only when the hub transport survived run-narrowing; E1-loud when the hub wires without a `mainMailbox` resolver), then the `SubagentManager` → A2A gateway (a2a transport) → heartbeat (started, kill-switch aware) → `TaskToolConfig` (children draw the child-safe core list; live stream/model accessors) → monitoring tools → `task`, gated by `HostCapability.messagingFabric`/`HostCapability.subagents`.
- **Registry order preserved byte-identically**: `buildAgentStack` now emits core tools → gated task surface (monitoring, then `task` LAST) → residual `additionalTools` — exactly the pre-conversion registration order. The gated surface stays OUT of `WiredAgentCore.tools` (children must never draw it; the executor strips only `task` itself).
- **Catalog corrections** — `subagents` now requires `{sessionRoot, subagentServices}`; `messagingFabric`'s file transport declares `sessionRoot` per-transport (a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer).
- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). Net: the shell lost ~140 lines of hand-rolled assembly.
- **AGENTS.md** — the host-shell wiring rule now names the builder-owned task complex (conventions invariant).

## Remaining (later slices, per the issue)

- Checkpoint/roles/queue/approval/redaction post-construction attachments into the builder (slice 4).
- Model-facing emission through the plan (prompt sections/help driven by `surfacedTokens`).
- Remaining host shells (macOS/iOS/Android/web/extension/Outlook) consume `wireAgentCore`; config-section parity (#1078) generalizes onto the builder per OQ1.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The main checkout's system dart is unusable here (flutter shim dies on seatbelt-blocked engine-stamp writes; the bare VM is SIGKILLed with exit 137 by the machine guard — the known lane pitfall). Gates ran in the worktree via a sibling lane's temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + the fleet `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`:

- `dart test test/hosts/ test/parity/` — **80/80 green** (matrix completeness, E1/E2, AC7 hiding, parity guards).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` — **87/87 green** (the CLI constructor end-to-end over the moved wiring).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_agents_panel_test.dart test/task/subagent_lifecycle_test.dart` — **36/36 green** (registry persistence/rehydration through the builder-assembled manager; child resume/wake).
- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart test/hosts` — clean. `dart format` applied (3.13.4; it reflowed two pre-existing spots in the hosts test/catalog that the previous slice's formatter version had left non-canonical).

New tests fail-first: the slice-3 group was written before the implementation (absent-bundle narrowing, child-safety of the core list, canonical order, fabric composition, handle exposure, off-profile hiding) and went green with the builder changes.

The question is: is there a path where the hub primary calls `mainMailbox` BEFORE `_subagentManager` is assigned? Since `_subagentManager = wired.subagentManager!` is assigned right after `wireAgentCore` returns, and the closure is only invoked at mail time, it should be fine. But what if the CLI profile has `subagents` off (e.g. a config where subagents capability is off) while hubFabric is provided? `off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface.

- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T09:54:56Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079

## Delivered (slice 3 — builder-owned jobs)

**The task/subagent/fabric complex moves into the capability-gated assembled set (PR #1230's first "Remaining" item); the CLI no longer passes `task`/monitoring as post-plan host tools nor hand-assembles the manager.**

- **`SubagentServices`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart`, new) — the typed bundle of genuinely shell-side glue: wake launcher, registry sink/source, heartbeat delivery + live thresholds, roles resolver, children's compaction choice, misuse-breaker switch, child-session factory, session-IO retry. Absent bundle = the capability run-narrows `off(reason: … subagentServices …)` like any missing platform service — the complex never half-wires.
- **`_wireFabric` / `_wireTaskSurface`** — the builder assembles the messaging fabric (file layer over `sessionRoot`; hub primary only when the hub transport survived run-narrowing; E1-loud when the hub wires without a `mainMailbox` resolver), then the `SubagentManager` → A2A gateway (a2a transport) → heartbeat (started, kill-switch aware) → `TaskToolConfig` (children draw the child-safe core list; live stream/model accessors) → monitoring tools → `task`, gated by `HostCapability.messagingFabric`/`HostCapability.subagents`.
- **Registry order preserved byte-identically**: `buildAgentStack` now emits core tools → gated task surface (monitoring, then `task` LAST) → residual `additionalTools` — exactly the pre-conversion registration order. The gated surface stays OUT of `WiredAgentCore.tools` (children must never draw it; the executor strips only `task` itself).
- **Catalog corrections** — `subagents` now requires `{sessionRoot, subagentServices}`; `messagingFabric`'s file transport declares `sessionRoot` per-transport (a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer).
- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). Net: the shell lost ~140 lines of hand-rolled assembly.
- **AGENTS.md** — the host-shell wiring rule now names the builder-owned task complex (conventions invariant).

## Remaining (later slices, per the issue)

- Checkpoint/roles/queue/approval/redaction post-construction attachments into the builder (slice 4).
- Model-facing emission through the plan (prompt sections/help driven by `surfacedTokens`).
- Remaining host shells (macOS/iOS/Android/web/extension/Outlook) consume `wireAgentCore`; config-section parity (#1078) generalizes onto the builder per OQ1.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The main checkout's system dart is unusable here (flutter shim dies on seatbelt-blocked engine-stamp writes; the bare VM is SIGKILLed with exit 137 by the machine guard — the known lane pitfall). Gates ran in the worktree via a sibling lane's temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + the fleet `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`:

- `dart test test/hosts/ test/parity/` — **80/80 green** (matrix completeness, E1/E2, AC7 hiding, parity guards).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` — **87/87 green** (the CLI constructor end-to-end over the moved wiring).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_agents_panel_test.dart test/task/subagent_lifecycle_test.dart` — **36/36 green** (registry persistence/rehydration through the builder-assembled manager; child resume/wake).
- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart test/hosts` — clean. `dart format` applied (3.13.4; it reflowed two pre-existing spots in the hosts test/catalog that the previous slice's formatter version had left non-canonical).

New tests fail-first: the slice-3 group was written before the implementation (absent-bundle narrowing, child-safety of the core list, canonical order, fabric composition, handle exposure, off-profile hiding) and went green with the builder changes.

capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface.

- **`SubagentServices`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart`, new) — the typed bundle of genuinely shell-side glue: wake launcher, registry sink/source, heartbeat delivery + live thresholds, roles resolver, children's compaction choice, misuse-breaker switch, child-session factory, session-IO retry. - **`_wireFabric` / `_wireTaskSurface`** — the builder assembles the messaging fabric (file layer over `sessionRoot`; hub primary only when the hub transport survived run-narrowing; E1-loud when the hub wires without a `mainMailbox` resolver), then the `SubagentManager` → A2A gateway (a2a transport) → heartbeat (started, kill-switch aware) → `TaskToolConfig` (children draw the child-safe core list; live stream/model accessors) → monitoring tools → `task`, gated by `HostCapability.messagingFabric`/`HostCapability.subagents`.

- **Catalog corrections** — `subagents` now requires `{sessionRoot, subagentServices}`; `messagingFabric`'s file transport declares `sessionRoot` per-transport (a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer).
- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). Net: the shell lost ~140 lines of hand-rolled assembly.
- **AGENTS.md** — the host-shell wiring rule now names the builder-owned task complex (conventions invariant).

## Remaining (later slices, per the issue)

- Checkpoint/roles/queue/approval/redaction post-construction attachments into the builder (slice 4).
- Model-facing emission through the plan (prompt sections/help driven by `surfacedTokens`).
- Remaining host shells (macOS/iOS/Android/web/extension/Outlook) consume `wireAgentCore`; config-section parity (#1078) generalizes onto the builder per OQ1.

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart test/hosts` — clean. `dart format` applied (3.13.4; it reflowed two pre-existing spots in the hosts test/catalog that the previous slice's formatter version had left non-canonical).

blocks.text:
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface.

  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 ruleset-
  bypass App pushes the bump straight to protected main, so the App identity

- **Branch**: `fix/1079-sdk-host-slice3` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +713
- **Deletions**: -252
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T09:54:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T09:54:56Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079

## Delivered (slice 3 — builder-owned jobs)

**The task/subagent/fabric complex moves into the capability-gated assembled set (PR #1230's first "Remaining" item); the CLI no longer passes `task`/monitoring as post-plan host tools nor hand-assembles the manager.**

- **`SubagentServices`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart`, new) — the typed bundle of genuinely shell-side glue: wake launcher, registry sink/source, heartbeat delivery + live thresholds, roles resolver, children's compaction choice, misuse-breaker switch, child-session factory, session-IO retry. Absent bundle = the capability run-narrows `off(reason: … subagentServices …)` like any missing platform service — the complex never half-wires.
- **`_wireFabric` / `_wireTaskSurface`** — the builder assembles the messaging fabric (file layer over `sessionRoot`; hub primary only when the hub transport survived run-narrowing; E1-loud when the hub wires without a `mainMailbox` resolver), then the `SubagentManager` → A2A gateway (a2a transport) → heartbeat (started, kill-switch aware) → `TaskToolConfig` (children draw the child-safe core list; live stream/model accessors) → monitoring tools → `task`, gated by `HostCapability.messagingFabric`/`HostCapability.subagents`.
- **Registry order preserved byte-identically**: `buildAgentStack` now emits core tools → gated task surface (monitoring, then `task` LAST) → residual `additionalTools` — exactly the pre-conversion registration order. The gated surface stays OUT of `WiredAgentCore.tools` (children must never draw it; the executor strips only `task` itself).
- **Catalog corrections** — `subagents` now requires `{sessionRoot, subagentServices}`; `messagingFabric`'s file transport declares `sessionRoot` per-transport (a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer).
- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). Net: the shell lost ~140 lines of hand-rolled assembly.
- **AGENTS.md** — the host-shell wiring rule now names the builder-owned task complex (conventions invariant).

## Remaining (later slices, per the issue)

- Checkpoint/roles/queue/approval/redaction post-construction attachments into the builder (slice 4).
- Model-facing emission through the plan (prompt sections/help driven by `surfacedTokens`).
- Remaining host shells (macOS/iOS/Android/web/extension/Outlook) consume `wireAgentCore`; config-section parity (#1078) generalizes onto the builder per OQ1.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The main checkout's system dart is unusable here (flutter shim dies on seatbelt-blocked engine-stamp writes; the bare VM is SIGKILLed with exit 137 by the machine guard — the known lane pitfall). Gates ran in the worktree via a sibling lane's temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + the fleet `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`:

- `dart test test/hosts/ test/parity/` — **80/80 green** (matrix completeness, E1/E2, AC7 hiding, parity guards).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` — **87/87 green** (the CLI constructor end-to-end over the moved wiring).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_agents_panel_test.dart test/task/subagent_lifecycle_test.dart` — **36/36 green** (registry persistence/rehydration through the builder-assembled manager; child resume/wake).
- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart test/hosts` — clean. `dart format` applied (3.13.4; it reflowed two pre-existing spots in the hosts test/catalog that the previous slice's formatter version had left non-canonical).

New tests fail-first: the slice-3 group was written before the implementation (absent-bundle narrowing, child-safety of the core list, canonical order, fabric composition, handle exposure, off-profile hiding) and went green with the builder changes.

`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface.

## PR Description

Part of #1079

## Delivered (slice 3 — builder-owned jobs)

**The task/subagent/fabric complex moves into the capability-gated assembled set (PR #1230's first "Remaining" item); the CLI no longer passes `task`/monitoring as post-plan host tools nor hand-assembles the manager.**

- **`SubagentServices`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart`, new) — the typed bundle of genuinely shell-side glue: wake launcher, registry sink/source, heartbeat delivery + live thresholds, roles resolver, children's compaction choice, misuse-breaker switch, child-session factory, session-IO retry. Absent bundle = the capability run-narrows `off(reason: … subagentServices …)` like any missing platform service — the complex never half-wires.
- **`_wireFabric` / `_wireTaskSurface`** — the builder assembles the messaging fabric (file layer over `sessionRoot`; hub primary only when the hub transport survived run-narrowing; E1-loud when the hub wires without a `mainMailbox` resolver), then the `SubagentManager` → A2A gateway (a2a transport) → heartbeat (started, kill-switch aware) → `TaskToolConfig` (children draw the child-safe core list; live stream/model accessors) → monitoring tools → `task`, gated by `HostCapability.messagingFabric`/`HostCapability.subagents`.
- **Registry order preserved byte-identically**: `buildAgentStack` now emits core tools → gated task surface (monitoring, then `task` LAST) → residual `additionalTools` — exactly the pre-conversion registration order. The gated surface stays OUT of `WiredAgentCore.tools` (children must never draw it; the executor strips only `task` itself).
- **Catalog corrections** — `subagents` now requires `{sessionRoot, subagentServices}`; `messagingFabric`'s file transport declares `sessionRoot` per-transport (a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer).
- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). Net: the shell lost ~140 lines of hand-rolled assembly.
- **AGENTS.md** — the host-shell wiring rule now names the builder-owned task complex (conventions invariant).

## Remaining (later slices, per the issue)

- Checkpoint/roles/queue/approval/redaction post-construction attachments into the builder (slice 4).
- Model-facing emission through the plan (prompt sections/help driven by `surfacedTokens`).
- Remaining host shells (macOS/iOS/Android/web/extension/Outlook) consume `wireAgentCore`; config-section parity (#1078) generalizes onto the builder per OQ1.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The main checkout's system dart is unusable here (flutter shim dies on seatbelt-blocked engine-stamp writes; the bare VM is SIGKILLed with exit 137 by the machine guard — the known lane pitfall). Gates ran in the worktree via a sibling lane's temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + the fleet `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`:

- `dart test test/hosts/ test/parity/` — **80/80 green** (matrix completeness, E1/E2, AC7 hiding, parity guards).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` — **87/87 green** (the CLI constructor end-to-end over the moved wiring).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_agents_panel_test.dart test/task/subagent_lifecycle_test.dart` — **36/36 green** (registry persistence/rehydration through the builder-assembled manager; child resume/wake).
- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart test/hosts` — clean. `dart format` applied (3.13.4; it reflowed two pre-existing spots in the hosts test/catalog that the previous slice's formatter version had left non-canonical).

New tests fail-first: the slice-3 group was written before the implementation (absent-bundle narrowing, child-safety of the core list, canonical order, fabric composition, handle exposure, off-profile hiding) and went green with the builder changes.

blocks.text:
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface.

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set

  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 ruleset-
  bypass App pushes the bump straight to protected main, so the App identity
  is what auditability hangs on.
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev

## PR Description

Part of #1079

## Delivered (slice 3 — builder-owned jobs)

**The task/subagent/fabric complex moves into the capability-gated assembled set (PR #1230's first "Remaining" item); the CLI no longer passes `task`/monitoring as post-plan host tools nor hand-assembles the manager.**

- **`SubagentServices`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart`, new) — the typed bundle of genuinely shell-side glue: wake launcher, registry sink/source, heartbeat delivery + live thresholds, roles resolver, children's compaction choice, misuse-breaker switch, child-session factory, session-IO retry. Absent bundle = the capability run-narrows `off(reason: … subagentServices …)` like any missing platform service — the complex never half-wires.
- **`_wireFabric` / `_wireTaskSurface`** — the builder assembles the messaging fabric (file layer over `sessionRoot`; hub primary only when the hub transport survived run-narrowing; E1-loud when the hub wires without a `mainMailbox` resolver), then the `SubagentManager` → A2A gateway (a2a transport) → heartbeat (started, kill-switch aware) → `TaskToolConfig` (children draw the child-safe core list; live stream/model accessors) → monitoring tools → `task`, gated by `HostCapability.messagingFabric`/`HostCapability.subagents`.
- **Registry order preserved byte-identically**: `buildAgentStack` now emits core tools → gated task surface (monitoring, then `task` LAST) → residual `additionalTools` — exactly the pre-conversion registration order. The gated surface stays OUT of `WiredAgentCore.tools` (children must never draw it; the executor strips only `task` itself).
- **Catalog corrections** — `subagents` now requires `{sessionRoot, subagentServices}`; `messagingFabric`'s file transport declares `sessionRoot` per-transport (a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer).
- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). Net: the shell lost ~140 lines of hand-rolled assembly.
- **AGENTS.md** — the host-shell wiring rule now names the builder-owned task complex (conventions invariant).

## Remaining (later slices, per the issue)

- Checkpoint/roles/queue/approval/redaction post-construction attachments into the builder (slice 4).
- Model-facing emission through the plan (prompt sections/help driven by `surfacedTokens`).
- Remaining host shells (macOS/iOS/Android/web/extension/Outlook) consume `wireAgentCore`; config-section parity (#1078) generalizes onto the builder per OQ1.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The main checkout's system dart is unusable here (flutter shim dies on seatbelt-blocked engine-stamp writes; the bare VM is SIGKILLed with exit 137 by the machine guard — the known lane pitfall). Gates ran in the worktree via a sibling lane's temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + the fleet `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`:

- `dart test test/hosts/ test/parity/` — **80/80 green** (matrix completeness, E1/E2, AC7 hiding, parity guards).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` — **87/87 green** (the CLI constructor end-to-end over the moved wiring).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_agents_panel_test.dart test/task/subagent_lifecycle_test.dart` — **36/36 green** (registry persistence/rehydration through the builder-assembled manager; child resume/wake).
- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart test/hosts` — clean. `dart format` applied (3.13.4; it reflowed two pre-existing spots in the hosts test/catalog that the previous slice's formatter version had left non-canonical).

New tests fail-first: the slice-3 group was written before the implementation (absent-bundle narrowing, child-safety of the core list, canonical order, fabric composition, handle exposure, off-profile hiding) and went green with the builder changes.

Very important finding! The **mobile profile declares `messagingFabric: CapabilityTransportState({'hub'}, 'no shared filesystem; hub-only messaging')`**. So the mobile profiles (ios/android) are exactly the hub-only case. `_wireFabric` bails (`return null`) when `!transports.contains('file') || services.sessionRoot == null` — meaning for mobile hosts (hub-only, no sessionRoot), `_wireFabric` returns null, the hub transport never wires even though the plan says it wires. That's a latent design gap: `_wireFabric` cannot assemble a hub-only fabric. The catalog correction in this PR explicitly says "a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer" — but `_wireFabric` doesn't just skip the file layer, it skips the ENTIRE fabric including the wired hub transport. Silent narrowing below the plan (no reason recorded) — exactly the "silent" behavior E1 exists to prevent. For the CLI (file+hub+a2a all default, sessionRoot always present), it doesn't bite today. It's worth an IMPORTANT finding: `_wireFabric` silently drops the whole capability when file transport is absent even if hub wires — should either throw E1-loud or narrow with a reason.

Wait, actually let me re-check: for the mobile profile, would run-narrowing drop 'hub' too if hubFabric absent? Mobile host would provide hubFabric (the hub plugin). If provided, transports = {hub} survive. `_wireFabric` → fabricPlan is WiredCapability({hub}); `!transports.contains('file')` → true → return null. The host gets `wired.fabric == null` with plan saying messagingFabric wired (hub). No exception, no reason. Silent divergence between plan and reality. Yes — legit IMPORTANT finding (future-slice impact; not CLI-affecting).

Also mobile profiles have `subagents: _inventoryRow('macOS app')` — inventory-driven, might be on. If a mobile host wires subagents ON (inventory says on) and provides a SubagentServices bundle, `_wireTaskSurface` would construct SubagentManager with `messaging: null` (fabric null). blocks.text:
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface.

- **Title**: feat(1079): SDK slice 3 — builder-owned task/subagent/fabric complex
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1079-sdk-host-slice3` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +713
- **Deletions**: -252
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T09:54:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T09:54:56Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079

## Delivered (slice 3 — builder-owned jobs)

**The task/subagent/fabric complex moves into the capability-gated assembled set (PR #1230's first "Remaining" item); the CLI no longer passes `task`/monitoring as post-plan host tools nor hand-assembles the manager.**

- **`SubagentServices`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart`, new) — the typed bundle of genuinely shell-side glue: wake launcher, registry sink/source, heartbeat delivery + live thresholds, roles resolver, children's compaction choice, misuse-breaker switch, child-session factory, session-IO retry. Absent bundle = the capability run-narrows `off(reason: … subagentServices …)` like any missing platform service — the complex never half-wires.
- **`_wireFabric` / `_wireTaskSurface`** — the builder assembles the messaging fabric (file layer over `sessionRoot`; hub primary only when the hub transport survived run-narrowing; E1-loud when the hub wires without a `mainMailbox` resolver), then the `SubagentManager` → A2A gateway (a2a transport) → heartbeat (started, kill-switch aware) → `TaskToolConfig` (children draw the child-safe core list; live stream/model accessors) → monitoring tools → `task`, gated by `HostCapability.messagingFabric`/`HostCapability.subagents`.
- **Registry order preserved byte-identically**: `buildAgentStack` now emits core tools → gated task surface (monitoring, then `task` LAST) → residual `additionalTools` — exactly the pre-conversion registration order. The gated surface stays OUT of `WiredAgentCore.tools` (children must never draw it; the executor strips only `task` itself).
- **Catalog corrections** — `subagents` now requires `{sessionRoot, subagentServices}`; `messagingFabric`'s file transport declares `sessionRoot` per-transport (a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer).
- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). Net: the shell lost ~140 lines of hand-rolled assembly.
- **AGENTS.md** — the host-shell wiring rule now names the builder-owned task complex (conventions invariant).

## Remaining (later slices, per the issue)

- Checkpoint/roles/queue/approval/redaction post-construction attachments into the builder (slice 4).
- Model-facing emission through the plan (prompt sections/help driven by `surfacedTokens`).
- Remaining host shells (macOS/iOS/Android/web/extension/Outlook) consume `wireAgentCore`; config-section parity (#1078) generalizes onto the builder per OQ1.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The main checkout's system dart is unusable here (flutter shim dies on seatbelt-blocked engine-stamp writes; the bare VM is SIGKILLed with exit 137 by the machine guard — the known lane pitfall). Gates ran in the worktree via a sibling lane's temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + the fleet `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`:

- `dart test test/hosts/ test/parity/` — **80/80 green** (matrix completeness, E1/E2, AC7 hiding, parity guards).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` — **87/87 green** (the CLI constructor end-to-end over the moved wiring).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_agents_panel_test.dart test/task/subagent_lifecycle_test.dart` — **36/36 green** (registry persistence/rehydration through the builder-assembled manager; child resume/wake).
- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart test/hosts` — clean. `dart format` applied (3.13.4; it reflowed two pre-existing spots in the hosts test/catalog that the previous slice's formatter version had left non-canonical).

New tests fail-first: the slice-3 group was written before the implementation (absent-bundle narrowing, child-safety of the core list, canonical order, fabric composition, handle exposure, off-profile hiding) and went green with the builder changes.

- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). **Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)

a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers

- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T09:54:56Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079

## Delivered (slice 3 — builder-owned jobs)

**The task/subagent/fabric complex moves into the capability-gated assembled set (PR #1230's first "Remaining" item); the CLI no longer passes `task`/monitoring as post-plan host tools nor hand-assembles the manager.**

- **`SubagentServices`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart`, new) — the typed bundle of genuinely shell-side glue: wake launcher, registry sink/source, heartbeat delivery + live thresholds, roles resolver, children's compaction choice, misuse-breaker switch, child-session factory, session-IO retry. Absent bundle = the capability run-narrows `off(reason: … subagentServices …)` like any missing platform service — the complex never half-wires.
- **`_wireFabric` / `_wireTaskSurface`** — the builder assembles the messaging fabric (file layer over `sessionRoot`; hub primary only when the hub transport survived run-narrowing; E1-loud when the hub wires without a `mainMailbox` resolver), then the `SubagentManager` → A2A gateway (a2a transport) → heartbeat (started, kill-switch aware) → `TaskToolConfig` (children draw the child-safe core list; live stream/model accessors) → monitoring tools → `task`, gated by `HostCapability.messagingFabric`/`HostCapability.subagents`.
- **Registry order preserved byte-identically**: `buildAgentStack` now emits core tools → gated task surface (monitoring, then `task` LAST) → residual `additionalTools` — exactly the pre-conversion registration order. The gated surface stays OUT of `WiredAgentCore.tools` (children must never draw it; the executor strips only `task` itself).
- **Catalog corrections** — `subagents` now requires `{sessionRoot, subagentServices}`; `messagingFabric`'s file transport declares `sessionRoot` per-transport (a hub-only host without a session root no longer silently promises the file layer).
- **`WiredAgentCore` exposes the handles** (`fabric`, `fileFabric`, `messagesRoot`, `subagentManager`, `a2aManager`, `subagentHeartbeat`, `taskConfig`) — the CLI (`AgentCli`) keeps `/agents`, wake, mailbox and job-manager behavior unchanged, passing only callbacks (registry persistence closures, `_launchMailboxWake`, `_deliverHeartbeatDigest`, child-session minting over `_repo`). Net: the shell lost ~140 lines of hand-rolled assembly.
- **AGENTS.md** — the host-shell wiring rule now names the builder-owned task complex (conventions invariant).

## Remaining (later slices, per the issue)

- Checkpoint/roles/queue/approval/redaction post-construction attachments into the builder (slice 4).
- Model-facing emission through the plan (prompt sections/help driven by `surfacedTokens`).
- Remaining host shells (macOS/iOS/Android/web/extension/Outlook) consume `wireAgentCore`; config-section parity (#1078) generalizes onto the builder per OQ1.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

The main checkout's system dart is unusable here (flutter shim dies on seatbelt-blocked engine-stamp writes; the bare VM is SIGKILLed with exit 137 by the machine guard — the known lane pitfall). Gates ran in the worktree via a sibling lane's temp Dart SDK 3.13.4 + the fleet `$TMPDIR/fah-pub-cache`:

- `dart test test/hosts/ test/parity/` — **80/80 green** (matrix completeness, E1/E2, AC7 hiding, parity guards).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` — **87/87 green** (the CLI constructor end-to-end over the moved wiring).
- `dart test test/cli/agent_agents_panel_test.dart test/task/subagent_lifecycle_test.dart` — **36/36 green** (registry persistence/rehydration through the builder-assembled manager; child resume/wake).
- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart test/hosts` — clean. `dart format` applied (3.13.4; it reflowed two pre-existing spots in the hosts test/catalog that the previous slice's formatter version had left non-canonical).

New tests fail-first: the slice-3 group was written before the implementation (absent-bundle narrowing, child-safety of the core list, canonical order, fabric composition, handle exposure, off-profile hiding) and went green with the builder changes.

`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **State**: open
